title: Signed shift laws for a normalized reindexing comparison
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension in universe $u$. For each scheme $W$ in universe $u$, use either the positive finite coefficient sheaf $(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1})_W$ at $s=\mathrm{some}(n)$ or the ordinary completed ring sheaf $\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1})_W$ at $s=\mathrm{none}$ [lem-pod-reindexing-hom-resolution-model]. Write $D_W$ for its ordinary unbounded module derived category, $F_g$ for the recorded exact reindexing functor, and $H_W$ for the recorded derived Hom. Fix on every scheme in question a closed structure $S_W$ for $H_W$ and its normalized K-flat tensor model $T_W$ [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Assume $\ell$ is invertible in every residue field of every such scheme, and each pro-etale site is essentially small in universe $u+1$ (its object universe is $u+1$, its arrow universe is $u$, the module universe is $u+1$, and the localization universe is $u+2$). Let $g:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be a scheme isomorphism and let $c$ be any normalized Comparison [def-pod-reindexing-coherence-data]. There are ChainShift presentations on $X,Y$ satisfying ShiftLaws for $c$. Thus the componentwise chain comparison commutes with the double-shift isomorphism having scalar $(-1)^{ar}$ in degree $r$, and its derived comparison commutes with the specified signedShift, for all integers $a,b$. The derived shifts are the normalized ones of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction].

proof.text: Construct the double-shift map by reindexing p to p-a and multiplying by (-1)^(a*r). Consecutive degree scalars differ by (-1)^a, which compensates the source shift sign in both Hom differential terms. Reverse the reindexing with the same scalar for its inverse. Apply each Hom-product projection to the reindexing square: both routes have the same scalar and component by chain_projection and the identity degreewise shift comparison.

Shifted K-injective targets remain K-injective by shifting a map from an acyclic complex back, null-homotoping it and shifting the homotopy with (-1)^b. Apply derived_model to these targets. The right and left derived Hom shifts are characterized by the same signed product projections and augmentation equations, so localizing the chain square gives precisely signedShift. Use naturality along resolutions for arbitrary derived objects.
